Hi Dora! I'm Emma Johnson from Blue Sparrow Tech. I took a look at your personal website (www.dora-website.com) and wanted to share some feedback.

What works well:
- It's clean and straightforward — you get straight to the point about who the site belongs to, and your contact email is easy to find.
- For a personal site, that simplicity is a real strength; it loads fast and doesn't distract the visitor.

Suggestions to make it even stronger:
- Add a short intro about who you are and what you do — a couple of sentences on your background, work, or interests would give visitors an immediate sense of your personality.
- Consider a small portfolio or projects section with brief descriptions and links. Even three or four bullet points would make the site feel more substantial.
- A "About" page with a photo, plus links to your LinkedIn or other profiles, would help people connect the site to the rest of your presence.
- If you write or create anything, a small blog or notes section would give people a reason to come back.
- Adding a few recent posts with dates would make it clear the site is active and maintained.

Overall, it's a nice, no-fuss starting point — the foundation is there, and a bit more personality and content would really make it shine. Nice work!

Best,
Emma Johnson
Blue Sparrow Tech

Hi Eve! I'm Emma Johnson from Blue Sparrow Tech. I visited your blog (www.eve-blog.com) and wanted to share some feedback.

What works well:
- The site has a clear identity — you immediately get a sense of who you are and what you're passionate about (hiking is a great hook, and it's the kind of topic people genuinely enjoy reading about).
- It's approachable and easy to get into.

Suggestions to make it even stronger:
- Add actual blog posts! Right now the site reads more like a landing page than a blog. Even a couple of short entries about your recent hikes — trail notes, photos, gear tips, or a "best of" roundup — would give visitors something to actually read and share.
- Organize the content with categories or tags (e.g., trail reviews, gear, trip reports) so readers can easily find what interests them.
- Photos are everything for a hiking blog. Adding images with captions and alt text would make it far more engaging and accessible.
- An archive or "recent posts" list would help people discover older entries.
- A short bio and links to your socials would let readers follow along with your adventures.
- If you post regularly, a subscribe option (RSS or email) would help build a returning audience.

Overall, the topic is a great fit for a blog and the site has a warm, personal feel. With a few real posts and some photos, it could become a really enjoyable corner of the internet. Keep up the good work!

Best,
Emma Johnson
Blue Sparrow Tech
